## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Sabbaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative located in the Therāpadāna collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the spiritual biography and past meritorious deeds of the elder (thera) Sabbaphaladāyaka. SuttaCentral records five translations of the work across five different languages [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus indicates extensive formulaic connections within the Pali corpus, identifying 157 matching passages across 50 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal reuse occurs with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (first volume), which shares 42 matches with a substantial parallel sequence between segments §0.3–25.1 [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, the text shares standard formulaic closing verses (notably around segments §24.1–29.1) with numerous other fruit-offering apadānas, including the *Tālaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 511), *Pilakkhaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 386), *Vallikāraphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 480), and *Piyālaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 502) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali literature, DharmaNexus automatically computes tentative alignments with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-4) and the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) and *Saṃyukta Āgama* (T 99), though these reflect automated matches rather than curated parallels [DharmaNexus].
